artDirectionRequirements.authority: User direction, 2026-09-19; see the composition, identity and scale section of the plan.
artDirectionRequirements.scope: Remaining-continent proposals; existing approved artwork is not reopened.
artDirectionRequirements.FAR: One recognizable local landmark or dominant natural formation, readable in the runtime composite behind MID and away from repeat joins.
artDirectionRequirements.MID: One restrained, unique local sign of life: settlement/frontage, everyday-use detail or static background wildlife. No people or gameplay hazards baked into scenery.
artDirectionRequirements.originality: Compare identities and visible silhouettes against existing and proposed campaign elements. No reused species/objects, renamed duplicates or recolors as new hazards; shared background materials are not signature elements.
artDirectionRequirements.scale: Judge visible subjects at 960x540 and normal mobile presentation relative to characters, architecture and depth. Reject subjects that read too small or need implausible enlargement. Preserve canonical transforms and physics.
artDirectionRequirements.selectionReviewStatus: Africa agent selections resolved; remaining nine proposals still need campaign comparison. Visual size/reference inspection remains stage-specific.
artDirectionRequirements.approval: Requirements and workflow direction approved. Unresolved selection changes remain review items; generated artwork still requires deployed-stage acceptance.

execution.imageCalls: One built-in image generation call per physical output file; parallel image throughput is unmeasured. Sequential generation is permitted while independent preparation or QA runs in parallel.
execution.context: Fresh scoped worker context; selected stage/job and actual reference pixels only. Return a compact result manifest and exceptions, not raw logs.
execution.skillPolicy: Use the existing imagegen skill and repository resolver; no duplicate project skill added.
execution.pilot: Africa AF01–AF03; AF01 is the first acceptance checkpoint, then AF02 and AF03. Measure the complete trial before increasing concurrency.

stages.label: Tanzania — Serengeti savannah
stages.palette: Ochre, muted gold, olive and sky blue; turquoise bird accents.

FAR.direction: Warm open plains, low distant kopjes and a broad blue sky; scenery continues behind MID openings.

MID.direction: Widely spaced flat-topped acacias, golden grass islands and weathered rock groups; open sightlines and authored lower overlap.

GROUND.direction: Level compacted ochre trail with sparse dry grass at its edge and deep earth below; no baked obstacles.

GROUND1.label: Termite mound
GROUND1.direction: Compact taller mound with a clear triangular profile

GROUND2.label: Crested porcupine
GROUND2.direction: Low crouched side-on animal with a fan of banded quills; static, no attack animation or projectiles. Keep the core body much lower than the character; no giant mammal.

stages.referenceStatus: Six retrieved, inspected and hash-verified photographs plus approved game-style references. See assets/references/africa/af01/REFERENCES.json; attach only the selected output references.
stages.notes: Regional Tanzania/savanna species selection; no exact park occurrence claim. Porcupine may rest beside a shaded burrow because it is nocturnal. Large wildlife remains background-only. No log replacement by recoloring.

brief.farFocalPoint: A prominent granite kopje with a recognizable stacked-rock silhouette above the savannah.
brief.midLifeDetail: A restrained giraffe browsing an acacia away from the playable route.
campaignDistinctiveness: Termite mound: tapering earth tower, not an angular rock. Porcupine: low body/quill fan, not a log or llama. Roller: single bird with lilac breast/turquoise wings, not a parrot flock.
brief.intendedRelativeScale: The kopje must retain visual mass behind MID; the giraffe should read as a large animal at middle distance, not a miniature beside a tree. Hazard size is judged relative to the actual character; no fixed pixel dimensions are accepted before composite review. Small bird bodies remain smaller than characters; stork wings may exceed character height at the same apparent depth.

selectionReview: Agent compared candidate identities and silhouettes with all nine existing stages and the remaining proposed families. Artwork and measured scale still require deployed-stage acceptance.

referenceSources.credit: Stolz Gary M, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service

stages.label: Namibia — Sossusvlei dunes
stages.palette: Rust, terracotta, pale cream and cool blue; dark bird silhouette.

FAR.direction: Sweeping rust-orange dunes with pale distant ridges and clear sky; no savannah scene copied into this desert.

MID.direction: Sparse weathered dead-tree silhouettes, dune shoulders and pale clay-pan patches, with enough lower frontage for overlap.

GROUND.direction: Flat firm sand/clay trail with stratified ochre depth; dune slopes remain scenery rather than changing the running surface.

GROUND1.label: Curled clay-pan crust plates
GROUND1.direction: Low thin curled polygonal clay plates with open cracks; stylized shallow trip obstacle, not a solid stone block or oversized geological cliff.

GROUND2.label: Forked dead camelthorn snag
GROUND2.direction: Upright sparse Y-shaped branch with open negative space; no horizontal log, dense root ball or boulder base.

stages.referenceStatus: Source pages and initial image URLs researched; actual inspected per-output reference pack remains required. Direct HTTP retrieval was unavailable in the preparation environment; no downloaded/verified pixels are claimed.
stages.notes: Desert-edge Namibia species selection; no exact Sossusvlei sighting claim. Clay-plate exaggeration is an authored game prop, not a claimed measured geological feature. Keep the hazard low and avoid a boulder silhouette.

brief.farFocalPoint: One dominant high dune crest, with a clear sunlit face and shadow edge.
brief.midLifeDetail: A single oryx near sparse dead camelthorn silhouettes, well behind gameplay.
campaignDistinctiveness: Thin pale curled plates vs existing solid rocks; forked vertical snag vs existing horizontal log/root mass; compact sandgrouse avoids the goshawk/eagle silhouette repeat.
brief.intendedRelativeScale: Dune height and distance must read clearly; keep oryx anatomy and proportions plausible relative to nearby vegetation. Hazard size is judged relative to the actual character; no fixed pixel dimensions are accepted before composite review. Small bird bodies remain smaller than characters; stork wings may exceed character height at the same apparent depth.

selectionReview: Agent compared candidate identities and silhouettes with all nine existing stages and the remaining proposed families. Artwork and measured scale still require deployed-stage acceptance.

referenceSources.credit: Alan Manson, CC BY-SA 2.0; appearance reference photographed in South Africa, not Sossusvlei
